_comment: Reviewed ABI identities for the macOS 27.3 (26C5035r) kernelcache, pinned to that exact image.
Everything here was identified from the chip's own bytes; the evidence field says how. Two entries
were added after hardware round b141: the kernel booted, AppleImage4 loaded, and it called through a
__DATA_CONST slot that prelink emission had stubbed, which is what the fileset unmapped-call guard
reports as 'original component called an unmapped kernel function'. The two targets are ordinary
kernel functions this tree does build; the matcher simply could not pair them, because both are the
kind of three-instruction forwarder its shape methods have nothing to bite on, and both symbol names
are duplicated in the native kernel (each also carries an _external alias at another address), which
keeps them out of named_functions. Pairing them removes four stub sites across three kexts.

functions.evidence: Typed kalloc entry: materialises 0xD1000 (mov w9,#4096; movk w9,#13,lsl#16), loads the zone pointer from [x0], merges the low three bits of w1 into the size with and w10,w1,#0x7 / orr w2,w10,w9, and dispatches on whether the zone pointer is null. The native function at 0xfffffff007364b28 is the same shape instruction for instruction except that Apple's build inlines the per-CPU zone peek (mrs x11,TPIDR_EL1; ldrh w11,[x11,#440]; add x11,x1,x11,lsl#14) where this tree calls out. Position agrees: it sits between _kalloc_data_require and _kalloc_type_var_impl in the original, as in osfmk/kern/kalloc.c. The other native symbol of that name (0xfffffff00754d388) opens with mov w1,#4 and b, and is not this function. Referenced by __DATA_CONST slots in com.apple.security.AppleImage4 (0xfffffff00814de80), com.apple.driver.AppleMobileFileIntegrity (0xfffffff0081d4288) and, in the boot that exposed it, an indirect call from AppleImage4 __TEXT_EXEC+0xee0c.

Three instructions: bti c; orr x0,x0,#1; b <kfree_type_impl_internal>. The native function at 0xfffffff007365020 is byte-identical in shape (bti c; orr x0,x0,#1; b) and is the same twelve bytes long, which is the whole function: the original's next function, _kfree_data, starts at 0xfffffe000bb2c750, exactly as _kfree_data starts at 0xfffffff00736502c after the native one. It sits between _kfree_type_impl and _kfree_data in both images, matching the order in osfmk/kern/kalloc.c. The other native symbol of that name (0xfffffff007adb020) is a stack-framed wrapper with three calls and is not this function. Referenced by __DATA_CONST slots in com.apple.driver.AppleARMWatchdogTimer (0xfffffff007fbc468) and com.apple.driver.AppleMobileFileIntegrity (0xfffffff0081d42c8).
